newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa rockets on better-than-expected profit.
newsitem.headline: Axa rockets on better-than-expected profit.

text.p: Shares in French insurance group Axa shot higher on Wednesday after the company reported a bigger than expected jump in net attributable profit to 1.98 billion francs from 1.30 billion for the first half.
"The results were significantly better than expected," a trader said.
"Axa is the best insurance stock in the market," said another trader, who added that the stock was also well oriented in the technical charts.
Axa shares were up 10.50 francs, or 3.67 percent, at 296.50 at 0920 GMT. The bourse's CAC-40 index was up 0.7 percent.
Axa, which has been spared the ravages in the property market dragging down other financial groups, forecast average annual earnings per share growth above 15 percent to the year 2000.
Chairman Claude Bebear told an analysts' meeting on Wednesday that he expected a good second half but that it would "be a bit optimistic" to expect it to match the first half".
